title: The Initiation of Force
summary: Why starting the use of physical force is the basic political evil.

lessons.title: What physical force is
lessons.objective: Name physical force as compulsion against a person’s body or property, not as a strong opinion.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what is physical force?

choices.text: Compulsion against a person’s body or property
Any argument spoken in a loud voice
Any loss someone feels after a deal
Any idea that loses a vote

feedback.note: Physical force here means making someone act by seizing the body or what the person owns, not by winning an argument.

exercises.prompt: Match each act to whether it is physical force.

pairs.left: Locking a person in a room

feedback.note: Force acts on body or property. Words and refusals do not become force just because they sting.

exercises.prompt: Complete the definition used in this lesson.

parts.text: Physical force compels a person through the

feedback.note: The two targets of physical force in politics are the person’s body and the person’s property.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states what persuasion does instead of force.

feedback.note: Persuasion leaves the other person free to say yes or no. Force does not.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is physical force?

choices.text: Taking a wallet out of someone’s hand
Publishing an essay the owner dislikes
Offering a price the seller rejects
Walking away from a conversation

feedback.note: Taking the wallet uses the other person’s property without consent. The other three leave body and property untouched.

exercises.prompt: Why is a bitter insult not physical force?

choices.text: It still leaves the hearer free to judge and act
Insults are always kind in politics
Only a written law can be force
Force exists only when a crowd does it

feedback.note: An insult can be wrong in other ways, but it does not replace the hearer’s control of body or property.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to the idea it names in this lesson.

pairs.right: What a person owns and controls

feedback.note: Compulsion overrides choice. Persuasion addresses it. Property is one of the things force can seize.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

feedback.note: People can argue and still each keep control of themselves. Force ends that.

exercises.prompt: Order the tokens into the lesson’s rule.

feedback.note: The mark of physical force is that the victim’s choice no longer decides what happens to body or property.

exercises.prompt: Which pair both count as physical force?

choices.text: A beating and a confiscation of tools
A rumor and a bad review
A high price and a low bid
Silence and leaving the room

feedback.note: Hitting the body and taking the tools are the same kind of act: compulsion. Talk and trade offers are not.

lessons.title: Who starts it
lessons.objective: Separate the person who starts force from the person who uses force only to stop it.

exercises.prompt: Who initiates force?

choices.text: The person who first uses force against another
The person who stops an attack already underway
Whoever speaks first in a dispute
Whoever has more money in the dispute

feedback.note: Initiation means being the one who starts the use of force. Answering an attack is not the start.

exercises.prompt: Match each role to the right description.

pairs.right: Has force used against them first
Uses force only to stop the attack

feedback.note: The moral difference in this unit is who started it, not who is stronger when it ends.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: Starting force is the evil. Force used only to

feedback.note: Defensive force answers a force that someone else already started. It does not open a new attack.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about the order of acts.

feedback.note: The start is the first use of force. Later force that only blocks that start is a different act.

exercises.prompt: A mugger grabs a bag. The owner pulls it back and shoves the mugger off. Who initiated force?

choices.text: The mugger
The owner
Both equally, because both used their hands
Neither, because no law was read aloud

feedback.note: The grab started the force. Pulling the bag back and shoving the attacker off answers that start.

exercises.prompt: What makes retaliatory force different from initiation?

choices.text: It comes after force has already been started, and aims to stop it
It is always gentler than the first blow
It is hidden so the starter never notices
It is done only to make a profit

feedback.note: Retaliation is a response. Its point is to end the force that someone else began, not to open a new one.

exercises.prompt: Match the act to the label.

pairs.left: Breaking into a shop at night
The same guard later looting a closed shop

feedback.note: Stopping the break-in answers force. Looting a different shop starts a new use of force.

exercises.prompt: Fill the rule about who is responsible for the start.

parts.text: the force is the one who

feedback.note: Responsibility for initiation tracks the first use, not the later effort to end it.

exercises.prompt: Two people trade insults, then one throws a punch. What started the force?

choices.text: The punch
The first insult
The topic they argued about
Anyone who heard them

feedback.note: Insults are not physical force. The punch is the start of force in that scene.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names the basic political evil in this unit.

feedback.note: The evil named here is the start of physical force, not the act of stopping that start.

lessons.title: Why it is basic
lessons.objective: Explain why starting force is the basic political evil: it replaces the victim’s judgment with compulsion.

exercises.prompt: Why is starting force called the basic political evil?

choices.text: It swaps the victim’s judgment for the starter’s compulsion
It is the rudest tone a person can use
It is rare, so it matters more than common wrongs
It is the only act a tax form can describe

feedback.note: Politics is about how people deal with one another. Starting force ends dealing by judgment and puts compulsion in its place.

exercises.prompt: Match each way of dealing with others to its result.

pairs.right: A mistake, not yet a political attack

feedback.note: A private mistake can be wrong without being the basic political evil. Starting force is that evil because it rules another person.

exercises.prompt: Complete the idea.

parts.text: Started force makes the victim act by

feedback.note: The victim may still have a mind, but the starter will not let that mind decide what happens.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about social life.

feedback.note: The alternative to started force is dealing by persuasion and voluntary exchange, where each person still chooses.

exercises.prompt: A person lies to himself about a fact and harms only his own plan. Is that the basic political evil?

choices.text: No. It is a private error, not the start of force against someone else
Yes. Every error is the basic political evil
Yes, if anyone later hears about the error
Only if a committee disagrees with the plan

feedback.note: Political evil in this unit is about force between people. A self-contained mistake does not initiate force.

exercises.prompt: What does the initiator take from the victim that persuasion does not?

choices.text: Control over the victim’s own action
A pleasant mood for the rest of the day
The right to pick the topic of a chat
A preferred style of speech

feedback.note: Persuasion can change a mind only if the person accepts it. Force takes the decision away.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to its meaning.

pairs.right: The root political wrong, not a side complaint
About how people deal with one another

feedback.note: Calling it basic means other political wrongs trace back to someone starting force, not to mere disagreement.

exercises.prompt: Fill the blanks.

feedback.note: That substitution is why the start of force is not just a private flaw. It rules another person.

exercises.prompt: Order the tokens.

feedback.note: Voluntary action is action the person chose. Started force is the block on that.

exercises.prompt: Which scene shows the basic political evil of this unit?

choices.text: A gang takes a farmer’s crop so he must obey them
A farmer miscounts his own seed and plants too little
A buyer offers less than the farmer hoped
A neighbor writes a poem the farmer finds ugly

feedback.note: The raid starts force and replaces the farmer’s judgment about his crop. The other scenes do not.

lessons.title: Fraud and threats
lessons.objective: Treat fraud and a credible threat of force as ways of starting force, not as clever exceptions.

exercises.prompt: Why does a credible threat count as starting force?

choices.text: The victim obeys to avoid harm to body or property
Threats are written in special ink
Every joke about harm is force
A threat counts only after an election

feedback.note: If the victim yields because force is promised against body or property, the force has already been started by the threat.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the right label.

pairs.left: Pay me or I burn your shop
Selling a painted rock as a gold coin
Saying the coin looks ugly but is real gold

feedback.note: A threat promises compulsion. Fraud takes property by a fake deal. A mere opinion about looks does neither.

exercises.prompt: Complete the account of fraud.

feedback.note: The victim would not hand the goods over if the facts of the deal were what they seemed. The consent is fake.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about a threat.

feedback.note: The harm need not land yet. Promising it so the victim yields is already the start.

exercises.prompt: A seller swaps an empty box for the full one after the buyer has paid, then keeps the money. What is that?

choices.text: Fraud, a way of starting force against property
Sharp skill that the buyer should admire
A difference of taste about packaging
A gift the buyer chose twice

feedback.note: The buyer consented to a full box. The swap takes the payment without that consent, which is fraud.

exercises.prompt: Which line is not a start of force?

choices.text: I will not buy your goods at that price
Pay me or I smash the goods
This deed is genuine, though the seller forged it
Sign this or you will be shot

feedback.note: Refusing a price leaves the other person’s body and property alone. The other three take or threaten them.

exercises.prompt: Match the indirect start to what it uses.

pairs.right: A promised harm if the victim does not yield
A fake fact that obtains a handover
Force already landing on body or goods

feedback.note: Direct force, threats, and fraud are three ways of starting the same evil. They differ in method, not in kind.

exercises.prompt: Fill the blanks.

parts.text: An empty boast is not force. A threat the victim must take as

feedback.note: The test is whether the victim is being made to yield to promised compulsion, not whether the words sound dramatic.

exercises.prompt: Order the tokens about fraud.

feedback.note: Without the fake, the handover would not happen. That is why fraud belongs with started force.

exercises.prompt: Someone says, Give me the keys or I will hurt you, and means it. The keys change hands. No blow lands. Did force start?

choices.text: Yes. The credible threat already started it
No. Force starts only when a blow lands
Only if the victim later feels sad
Only if the keys were made of iron

feedback.note: The victim gave up the keys to avoid the promised harm. Waiting for the blow would miss the start.

lessons.title: What is not a start of force
lessons.objective: Keep refusal, competition, error, and unwelcome speech outside the idea of starting force.

exercises.prompt: A shopper buys from a rival, so your sales fall. Did the shopper initiate force?

choices.text: No. Choosing another seller is not force
Yes. Any loss of sales is force
Yes, if you needed that sale badly
Yes, if it happens more than once a week

feedback.note: Competition can cost you a sale. It does not seize your body or your goods. The shopper’s money was never yours until a deal.

exercises.prompt: Match each act to the right class.

pairs.left: A calculation error in your own books

feedback.note: Loss, offense, and mistakes can be real without being the initiation of force. The threat that takes goods is that initiation.

exercises.prompt: Complete the distinction.

parts.text: A refusal leaves the other person’s
in place. A seizure takes that

feedback.note: Saying no does not reach into what the other person already has. Seizure does.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence about unwelcome speech.

feedback.note: Speech can be false, cruel, or unwanted and still not be the start of physical force.

exercises.prompt: Which act does initiate force?

choices.text: Locking a worker in until the worker signs
Hiring someone else for the job
Printing a harsh review of the work
Quitting a job you no longer want

feedback.note: Locking the worker in compels the signature. Hiring, reviewing, and quitting leave the other person’s body and property alone.

exercises.prompt: You are offered a deal and you say no. What did you do?

choices.text: You kept your own choice. You did not start force
You stole the offer by refusing it
You used force equal to a blow
You committed fraud by disagreeing

feedback.note: An offer is not an entitlement. Declining it is the ordinary opposite of force.

exercises.prompt: Match the feeling to the fact about force.

feedback.note: Feelings of loss or offense do not decide the question. The question is whether force against body or property was started.

exercises.prompt: Fill the summary line.

feedback.note: This unit keeps the evil narrow on purpose: the start of physical force, including fraud and real threats.

exercises.prompt: Order the closing rule.

feedback.note: Refusal is how a person keeps control. Treating it as force would erase the difference this unit teaches.

exercises.prompt: What is the basic political evil in this unit?

choices.text: Starting the use of physical force
Being less wealthy than a neighbor
Holding a false opinion in private
Speaking in plain words someone dislikes

feedback.note: Wealth gaps, private error, and disliked speech are not that evil. Starting physical force is.
